name: Building a Multi-Year Pavement Management Plan in Los Angeles County

mainEntity.name: What should property managers in Los Angeles County include in a multi-year pavement management plan for several properties?
mainEntity.text: What should property managers in Los Angeles County include in a multi-year pavement management plan for several properties?

acceptedAnswer.text: For property managers overseeing multiple sites in Los Angeles County, a structured pavement management plan can prevent crisis repairs and smooth budgets. Begin with a simple inventory: map driveways, parking lots, and internal roads at each property, noting age, material type, and visible issues. Use a basic condition rating (for example, excellent, good, fair, poor) to compare sites. Prioritize safety and liability concerns first, such as trip hazards, severe potholes, and drainage problems that cause ponding or ice in cooler areas. Then plan preventative maintenance like crack sealing and sealcoating on a regular cycle, focusing on assets in fair condition to prolong their life. For sections in poor condition or with base failures, schedule overlays or full reconstruction in specific years. Attach rough budget ranges to each project and group similar work across properties where possible to secure better pricing and reduce mobilization costs. Coordinate timing with tenants and businesses, avoiding peak seasons for retail centers or key resident events at multifamily properties. Partnering with a paving contractor willing to help update the plan annually ensures that pavement conditions and costs in Los Angeles County remain predictable rather than reactive.
acceptedAnswer.description: A multi-year pavement plan in Los Angeles County should inventory all paved areas, rate condition, prioritize safety issues, and schedule crack sealing, sealcoating, overlays, and replacements by year. Include budget estimates per property and coordinate with tenants to group work for volume pricing and minimal disruption.
